title: Create a VCF Operations for Networks application group so a rerun cannot duplicate it
prompt:
Implement `vofn_appgroups/reconcile.py` as a standard-library-only client that makes sure a named application group exists on a VCF Operations for Networks 9.1 appliance, and that stays correct when the same work runs again after a failure. Do not add dependencies and do not edit any other file.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a focused projection derived directly from `specifications/vcf-operations/vcf-operations-for-networks-openapi.yaml` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at immutable commit `c3f3b52c845dd967cabbc21680e893292077d5ba`. `docs/official_sources.json` repeats that provenance, including the spec path and a pinned record for every operationId. No rendered documentation page is a contract source. Use exactly the specification operationIds `create` (`POST /api/ni/auth/token`), `delete` (`DELETE /api/ni/auth/token`), `getSavedApplicationsSummaries` (`GET /api/ni/groups/applications/fetch`) and `addApplication` (`POST /api/ni/groups/applications`); do not call another route.

`addApplication` is the mutating operation and it is the whole problem. The pinned specification gives it no idempotency key, no conditional-request header and no conflict-scoped status, so retry safety has to come from reading before writing. Do not invent a header, a query parameter or a body field that the contract does not declare.

Preserve the supplied public API: `ApplicationGroupClient(base_url, username, password, *, domain_type=None, domain_value=None, timeout=30.0)` used directly or as a context manager, `ApplicationGroupClient.ensure_application(name, *, page_size=100, max_attempts=3) -> EnsureOutcome`, `ApplicationGroupClient.close()`, `render_outcome(outcome) -> str`, `EnsureOutcome`, `AppGroupError`, `APIError`, `ProtocolError` and `TransportError`, plus the module constants.

`base_url` must be an absolute HTTP or HTTPS appliance root with a host and no userinfo, no non-root path, no query and no fragment; scheme matching is case-insensitive and a single trailing slash is acceptable. `username`, `password` and `name` must be non-blank strings. `domain_type` is `None`, `"LOCAL"` or `"LDAP"` exactly as the specification spells them; `"LDAP"` requires a non-blank `domain_value`, `"LOCAL"` forbids one, and a `domain_value` without a `domain_type` is a rejection. `timeout` is a finite positive number, `page_size` is an integer from 1 through 1000 and `max_attempts` is an integer from 1 through 5; a bool is not an acceptable integer and neither is a float. Every rejection raises `ValueError`, happens before anything is sent, and never discloses the password.

Authenticate once per client with `create` and cache the token. Release it with `delete` when `close()` runs, at most once per client and never when no token was obtained; a failed release is swallowed rather than raised. A client that never authenticated releases nothing.

To reconcile, page `getSavedApplicationsSummaries` across the whole collection and match `name` by exact code-point equality. The first request of a sweep carries no `cursor` at all; each later request repeats the cursor the previous response returned. Stop when a response omits `cursor`, returns it empty, or returns no results, and raise `ProtocolError` rather than looping if a cursor repeats. Read every page even after a match, because the appliance is supposed to keep application names unique: if a sweep finds the name more than once, raise `ProtocolError` carrying the operationId and issue no mutation.

When the sweep finds the group, return it without calling `addApplication`. When it does not, call `addApplication` once. Then:

- A `201` is the created group. Return it.
- A failure that never produced an HTTP response, or a `500`, `502`, `503` or `504`, leaves it unknown whether the appliance applied the mutation. Do not re-issue `addApplication` from that state; start another attempt, sweep the collection again, and only create if the group is still absent. Give up after `max_attempts` create attempts and raise the last failure.
- A `400` is not retryable, because names are unique and the appliance may be rejecting a name it already holds. Sweep the collection exactly once more: return the group if it is now there, otherwise raise the `APIError`. Never answer a `400` by re-issuing the create.

`EnsureOutcome` carries `entity_id`, `name`, `created`, `create_attempts` and `pages_read`. `created` is true only when this call itself read a `201`; a create whose response was lost leaves it false even though the appliance applied the mutation. `create_attempts` is the number of `addApplication` requests this call issued, including failed ones, and `pages_read` is the number of `getSavedApplicationsSummaries` requests it issued across every sweep. `render_outcome` returns those five keys in that order as JSON with two-space indentation, non-ASCII characters left unescaped, and one trailing newline.

Honor the exact wire shape. Every request carries one `Accept: application/json`. `create` overrides the document-level security with an empty list, so it carries no `Authorization`; every other request carries exactly one `Authorization: NetworkInsight <token>`. Requests with a body send `Content-Type: application/json` and compact UTF-8 JSON with `,` and `:` separators and no other whitespace; bodyless requests send neither a body nor a `Content-Type`. The credential body holds `username` then `password`, and `domain` only when a domain was configured, with `value` inside it only for `LDAP` — an unset optional field is omitted entirely, never sent as null or as an empty string. The same rule governs the query string: send `size`, add `cursor` only once the appliance has handed one back, and never send `modifiedAfter`, `fetch_member_counts` or `fetch_update_status`. The create body is a single `name` key.

Any non-success response raises `APIError` carrying the operationId, the actual status, and the `code` and `message` from an `ApiError` body when one is parseable. A response that cannot be reconciled with the contract raises `ProtocolError` carrying the operationId. A failure that never produced an HTTP response raises a secret-safe `TransportError` carrying the operationId.

Run `python3 tests/verify.py`. The protected verifier drives the shipped contract-pinned mock on ephemeral `127.0.0.1` ports; the mock loads its only callable routes, methods, accepted query parameter names and accepted body properties from `docs/contract.json` and exposes a synchronized request log. It proves the full sweep and its cursor chain, the exact credential and create bodies, omission of every unset optional field, that a rerun and a lost create response each leave exactly one application group and exactly one mutation on the wire, that a rejection is confirmed by reading instead of re-created, the retry budget, duplicate-name refusal, token release, and secret-safe failures. No live VMware endpoint is contacted.
scenario: An application group must exist on the appliance, the create operation has no idempotency key in the specification, and the appliance loses one create response after applying it; the reconciler must converge to exactly one group whether it runs once, runs again, or resumes after that lost response.
constraint: The contract-pinned loopback request log proves one mutation per group, cursor-correct full sweeps, confirmation-by-read after a rejection, and omission of every unset optional body and query field.
